_about: Site-level corrections to module commentary, applied by tools/bundle.py to the bundled copy only (the module's export is untouched, and the loader then always uses the corrected chunk). Each entry replaces an exact text; the bundler warns when the text is no longer found, which means the module has fixed it and the entry can be removed.

network/commentary/nw-ban.json.why: The site's chance bar now uses the matched benchmark; the pooled figure overstates chance and is not shown anywhere.
network/commentary/nw-ban.json.find: Read the chart's "expected by chance" bar with care: it pools every window a contractor has, including approvals by offices that do not cover the recipient and filings that do not list the donor, so it reads high (the exporter's pooled figure for 2019-2025 records is 45%; the bar recomputes it for the records in view). Matched like with like, 19.4% of contributions would land in a window by chance, and 16.5% did.
network/commentary/nw-ban.json.replace: The "expected by chance" bar is matched like with like: it counts only the approvals that list the donor and whose approving office covered the recipient, with days weighted by the election calendar. On that basis 19.4% of contributions would land in a window by chance, and 16.5% did. A simpler benchmark that pools every window a contractor has, including approvals by offices that do not cover the recipient, reads much higher and overstates chance, so it is not used.

network/commentary/nw-ban.json.why: Live sentence: {expected_share} is now the matched benchmark.
network/commentary/nw-ban.json.find: ({inside_share}; the pooled chance benchmark for these records is {expected_share}, which overstates chance)
network/commentary/nw-ban.json.replace: ({inside_share}; over all years, matched like with like, {observed_matched} fell inside a window against {expected_share} expected by chance)

network/commentary/nw-ban.json.why: Caveat described the old pooled bar.
network/commentary/nw-ban.json.find: The "expected by chance" bar pools all of a contractor's windows and overstates chance; the matched benchmark in the analyst's read (19%) is the fair comparison.
network/commentary/nw-ban.json.replace: The "expected by chance" bar is the matched benchmark (19.4%) for all years; it rests on the approval-date proxy and the election-calendar weighting, and it does not change with your filters.

audits/commentary/au-overview.json.why: Red team 2: the site now computes impl_share over recommendations with a recorded follow-up status (as the finding does) and shows the no-status count; the template described the old all-rows computation.
audits/commentary/au-overview.json.find: {impl_share} of all of them are recorded as implemented (those never followed up count as not recorded); {open_fmt} were open or in progress at their last follow-up; median {median_months} months from report to recorded implementation.
audits/commentary/au-overview.json.replace: Of the {known_fmt} with a recorded follow-up status, {impl_share} are recorded as implemented ({nostatus_fmt} have no follow-up status and are left out of the rate); {open_fmt} were open or in progress at their last follow-up; median {median_months} months from report to recorded implementation, among the {timed_fmt} with a dated closure.

audits/commentary/au-overview.json.why: Paragraph described the old all-rows Implemented tile (40% unfiltered); the tile now uses the known-status denominator.
audits/commentary/au-overview.json.find: The Implemented tile divides by every matched recommendation, including those never followed up, so unfiltered it reads 40%; the rates in the finding use only recommendations with a recorded status.
audits/commentary/au-overview.json.replace: The Implemented tile and every rate on this dashboard use only recommendations with a recorded status, as the finding does, and each shows how many recommendations have none.

audits/commentary/au-overview.json.why: Rates now use recommendations with a recorded status; the view falls back when fewer than small_n of them match (e.g. BLA alone), so the fallback names that count.
audits/commentary/au-overview.json.find: Only {recs_fmt} recommendations match, too few for stable shares; widen the years or clear a filter.
audits/commentary/au-overview.json.replace: Only {known_fmt} of the {recs_fmt} matching recommendations have a recorded follow-up status, too few for stable shares; widen the years or clear a filter.

audits/commentary/au-status.json.why: Shares are now over recommendations with a recorded status (red team 2); no-status count shown separately.
audits/commentary/au-status.json.find: {recs_fmt} recommendations issued {years}, as shares of all of them: {impl_share} implemented, {prog_share} in progress, {open_share} open, {notimpl_share} will not be implemented; the rest were closed another way or have no follow-up status.
audits/commentary/au-status.json.replace: {recs_fmt} recommendations issued {years}; of the {known_fmt} with a recorded status, {impl_share} are implemented, {prog_share} in progress, {open_share} open and {notimpl_share} will not be implemented, and the rest were closed another way. {nostatus_fmt} have no follow-up status and are left out of these shares.

audits/commentary/au-status.json.why: Rates now use recommendations with a recorded status; the view falls back when fewer than small_n of them match (e.g. BLA alone), so the fallback names that count.
audits/commentary/au-status.json.find: Only {recs_fmt} recommendations match, too few for stable shares; widen the years or clear a filter.
audits/commentary/au-status.json.replace: Only {known_fmt} of the {recs_fmt} matching recommendations have a recorded follow-up status, too few for stable shares; widen the years or clear a filter.

audits/commentary/au-agreement.json.why: Response shares are now over recommendations with a recorded response, and impl_agreed / impl_disagreed over those with a recorded status (red team 2); the template described the old all-rows computation.
audits/commentary/au-agreement.json.find: {recs_fmt} recommendations issued {years}: {agree_share} agreed at publication, {partial_share} partially, {disagree_share} disagreed, and the rest printed no response. {impl_agreed} of the agreed and {impl_disagreed} of the disagreed are recorded as implemented (never followed up counts as not recorded).

Among those with a recorded follow-up status, {impl_agreed} of the agreed and {impl_disagreed} of the disagreed are recorded as implemented ({nostatus_fmt} have no follow-up status and are left out).

audits/commentary/au-time.json.why: The site now leaves the 651 inferred-implemented CSA rows (upper-bound date only) out of the step curves instead of counting them as never implemented (red team 2).
audits/commentary/au-time.json.find: The step curves count the 651 CSA recommendations closed by inference (no month count) as never implemented, so CSA curves read low.
audits/commentary/au-time.json.replace: The 651 CSA recommendations closed by inference (no month count, only a latest possible date) are left out of the step curves rather than counted as never implemented; leaving out these successes can make the affected cohorts read somewhat low at longer horizons.

audits/commentary/au-time.json.why: Same change: they are now also missing from the step curves.
